newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbekistan's grain harvest near end, below target.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekistan's grain harvest near end, below target.

text.p: Uzbekistan's grain harvest is near completion, with 2.84 million gross tonnes of grain reaped from 1.30 million hectares, or 90 percent of the sown area, a government official said on Friday.
"Harvesting will be over in about 10 days," an official from the ex-Soviet state's Macroeconomics and Statistics Ministry told Reuters. "The republic still has to gather grain from 120,000 hectares."
He said that at this time last year, the Central Asian state had harvested 2.65 million tonnes in bunker weight from 1.20 million hectares.
A total of 1.49 million hectares were sown to grain this year, below 1.69 million in 1996.
The official said grain yields have averaged 2.18 tonnes per hectare so far compared to last year's average of 2.19 tonnes.

Officials in Uzbekistan, a former Soviet republic with 23 million people, have targeted this year's grain harvest at 4.0 million tonnes, which would allow it to achieve much-desired self-sufficiency in grain.
But this year's harvest is likelty to fall far below the official target.

Trade sources predict Uzbekistan will probably remain a large grain buyer this year and say that last year, when the harvest was 3.54 million tonnes, the country still had to import about 1.60 million tonnes of wheat. --Shamil Baigin, Tashkent Newsroom, +7 371 1361958
